clue.text: Directions to a faithful friend to provide salt

parts.note: S and E are the compass points south and east
a dog is proverbially man's faithful friend

explanation.surface: Instructions for treating a loyal pet to a little salt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Salt' is not the seasoning but an old word for an experienced sailor.
explanation.definitionFit: An old salt and an old sea dog are both slang for a veteran sailor.

clue.text: Raised hat when introducing Oriental type

indicators.note: in a down clue, raising a word means reading it from the bottom up, so it runs backwards

parts.note: tile is slang for a hat
E stands for East, the Orient

explanation.surface: Someone lifts their hat on being introduced to a person from the East.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Raised' turns TILE into ELIT; 'when introducing' simply sets E after it.
explanation.definitionFit: Elite is a small typewriter typeface, twelve characters to the inch.

clue.text: Cease to live with artist — he's a dictator, of course

parts.note: to die is to stop living
Titian was the great Venetian painter

explanation.surface: A man who dies alongside a painter is revealed as a tyrant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Of course' puns on courses of a meal: this dictator rules what you eat.
explanation.definitionFit: A diet expert dictates what goes on the plate, course by course.

clue.text: Diminutive music-maker accompanying Lear's sagacious bird

definitions.text: Diminutive music-maker accompanying Lear's sagacious bird

parts.words: Diminutive music-maker accompanying Lear's sagacious bird
parts.note: in Edward Lear's poem The Owl and the Pussy-cat, the wise owl sings to a small stringed instrument

explanation.walkthrough: Lear here is the nonsense poet Edward Lear, not Shakespeare's king.
explanation.definitionFit: In the poem the Owl sang 'to a small' one of these stringed instruments.

clue.text: Refuse to give description of a person of influence

definitions.meaning: to keep back or decline to hand over

definitions.text: description of a person of influence
definitions.meaning: read as two words, someone ... over others has sway

explanation.definitionFit: To decline to hand something over; and, split in two, 'with hold' describes someone wielding power.

clue.text: Why this good Dane vandalized the plant

indicators.note: damaged and wrecked, so the four words are broken up and rebuilt

explanation.surface: A puzzled question about why a virtuous Dane wrecked a plant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vandalized' shuffles the fifteen letters of WHY THIS GOOD DANE.
explanation.definitionFit: This is bittersweet, a climbing poisonous plant of the potato family.

clue.text: It shows the limit of our liquidity

definitions.text: It shows the limit of our liquidity

parts.words: It shows the limit of our liquidity
parts.note: liquidity sounds financial, but here it is bath water, and the line left round the tub marks how high it came

explanation.walkthrough: 'Liquidity' suggests money; it is literally the water level of a bath or the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: A high-water line, left on a shore or round a bath, shows how far the water reached.

clue.text: Though only a villein, he has a parcel of land

parts.note: a lot is a plot or parcel of land

explanation.surface: A humble serf nonetheless owns a scrap of land.
explanation.definitionFit: A Spartan serf, a bondsman like the medieval villein.

clue.text: Hauled over the coals after material is torn

indicators.note: after means the scolding word follows the fabric word

parts.note: lace is a delicate fabric
to rate is an old verb meaning to scold severely

explanation.surface: Someone was severely reprimanded once the fabric got ripped.
explanation.walkthrough: RATE, to scold, is old-fashioned but still in dictionaries.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacerated means ripped or gashed, as torn flesh is.

clue.text: Controversial poet receives £1 for subsistence

indicators.note: receives means the poet's pair of words takes something into its middle

parts.note: a live issue is a hotly debated one
Thomas Hood was an English poet
L is the abbreviation for pound and I is one in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A provocative poet accepts a single pound to live on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Receives' puts L I between LIVE and HOOD.
explanation.definitionFit: One's means of support or living is one's subsistence.

clue.text: Many a typical expression from dwellers near this lake

parts.note: L is the Roman numeral for fifty, a crossword 'many'

parts.words: a typical expression from dwellers near this
parts.note: och is a stereotypical Scottish exclamation

explanation.surface: Locals by a certain lake have their characteristic way of speaking.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'dwellers near this lake' are Scots, whose exclamation 'och' follows L.
explanation.definitionFit: Loch is the Scottish word for a lake.

clue.text: Refinement of food

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both fineness or tact and a choice dish such as caviar.

clue.text: Dull river for grown-up

parts.note: matt or mat means not shiny
the Ure is a river in Yorkshire

explanation.surface: A boring stream suited to adults.
explanation.walkthrough: The URE is a Yorkshire river much loved by setters.
explanation.definitionFit: Grown-up and adult are synonyms of fully developed.

clue.text: Repulsive-sounding fruit

indicators.note: sounding says the word for repulsive is to be heard rather than spelt

parts.note: ugly means repulsive to look at

explanation.surface: A fruit whose name suggests it is hideous.
explanation.definitionFit: The ugli is a Jamaican citrus fruit, a tangelo with a wrinkled skin.

clue.text: Meeting-place where 13 had converted two students?

indicators.note: converted means changed into another form, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: the answer to 13 across, a citrus fruit
L, for learner, stands for a student; two of them

explanation.surface: A hall where a fruit was once turned into a pair of scholars.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Converted' rearranges UGLI plus HAD into GUILDHA; LL follows.
explanation.definitionFit: A guildhall is a civic building where a guild or town council meets.

clue.text: Needlewoman in barbaric rite?

indicators.note: in tells us the woman goes inside the scrambled word
barbaric suggests savagely mangled, so the word rite is rearranged

parts.note: Rita is a woman's name

explanation.surface: A seamstress takes part in a savage ritual.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Needlewoman' looks like one word but splits: NEEDLE is the definition and the woman is RITA; 'barbaric' turns RITE into IRTE, which takes RITA inside.
explanation.definitionFit: To needle someone is to annoy or provoke them.

clue.text: His interest in traffic worried Dean Smart

indicators.note: worried in the sense of shaken about, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A man named Dean Smart is anxious about road congestion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Traffic' means trade, not cars.
explanation.definitionFit: A shopkeeper or merchant makes a living from trading goods.

clue.text: Man overturned first-class carriage

parts.note: Victor is a man's name

indicators.note: in a down clue, overturned means turned upside down, so read upwards

parts.note: A1 means first-class, here written AI

explanation.surface: A man flipped a top-class railway coach.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Overturned' applies to A1 only, giving IA after VICTOR.
explanation.definitionFit: A victoria is a light four-wheeled horse-drawn carriage.

clue.text: Dine drunkenly, perhaps flounder about — monstrous!

indicators.note: about means the fish goes round the scrambled letters

parts.note: a flounder is one example of a fish

indicators.note: drunkenly suggests the word dine is reeling about, so it is rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone eats while drunk and flails about like a beast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drunkenly' turns DINE into ENDI, which 'about' puts inside FISH.
explanation.definitionFit: Fiendish means devilishly cruel, like a fiend or monster.

clue.text: Throws in a cutter, say

indicators.note: say tells us the tool's name is spoken rather than written

parts.note: an adze is a cutting tool for shaping wood

explanation.surface: Someone tosses in a blade, for example.
explanation.definitionFit: To throw in is to include or put in extra.

clue.text: Plant a halfwit in US Intelligence

indicators.note: in places the fool inside the agency

parts.note: the CIA is the US Central Intelligence Agency
an ass is a fool

explanation.surface: Planting a fool in the American spy agency.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plant' looks like a verb about spies; it is the definition, a shrub.
explanation.definitionFit: Cassia is a tropical shrub or tree, source of senna.

clue.text: Regulate publicity so much and no more

parts.note: an ad is an advertisement, publicity
just means exactly or only this much

explanation.surface: Controlling publicity so it is exactly enough.
explanation.definitionFit: To regulate a mechanism is to set it to the right level.

clue.text: Interest of union leader in American transport

indicators.note: in puts the first letter of union inside the other pieces

parts.note: RY is the abbreviation for railway

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A trade union boss takes an interest in US transport.
explanation.walkthrough: U from 'union leader' goes between US and RY.
explanation.definitionFit: Usury is lending money at interest, especially excessive interest.

clue.text: Ersatz sort of fuel base

parts.note: ersatz means fake, a sham

indicators.note: sort of means a kind or version of, so the letters of fuel are rearranged

explanation.surface: An artificial fuel used as a base.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Base' is not a foundation but an adjective meaning low or dishonourable.
explanation.definitionFit: Base conduct is low and dishonourable, deserving disgrace.

clue.text: Cavalryman retreating in an exceptional hurry!

indicators.note: retreating means going backwards, so the letters are read in reverse
in says the answer is concealed inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: A horse soldier falls back very quickly.
explanation.walkthrough: The run NALHU straddles 'exceptional hurry'; 'retreating' reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: An uhlan was a lancer in the Polish or Prussian cavalry.

clue.text: Ballads by university clerk

parts.note: the Bab Ballads are comic verses by W. S. Gilbert

explanation.surface: Songs written by a university clerk.
explanation.walkthrough: The Bab Ballads are W. S. Gilbert's comic poems.
explanation.definitionFit: Babu was a term in British India for a native clerk.

clue.text: Collect again and look like accepting a shilling

indicators.note: accepting means taking in, so the other letters go inside

parts.note: to resemble is to look like
S is the abbreviation for the old British shilling

explanation.surface: Someone gathers up again and appears to be taking a coin.
explanation.walkthrough: A shilling was a pre-decimal British coin, abbreviated S.
explanation.definitionFit: To gather things together once more is to bring them back together.

clue.text: Assume role of ship's officer, a childhood friend

parts.note: to play a part is to take on a role
a mate is an officer on a merchant ship

explanation.surface: Someone acts the part of a ship's officer opposite an old friend.
explanation.definitionFit: A child's companion in games is their playfellow.

clue.text: Shelter a Pole in part of the building

indicators.note: in places the pole inside the building part

parts.note: a wing is a section of a building
N is the North Pole

explanation.surface: A Polish man takes shelter in one wing of a building.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pole' looks like a Polish person; it is N, a magnetic pole.
explanation.definitionFit: An awning is a canvas cover giving shade or shelter.
